items.title: Recoverable pipeline understated by $64,248
items.body: Part 1 headlines ≈$142.8K. Summing the per-account figures Part 1 itself prints ($26,388 + $64,248 + $27,444.72 + $20,000 + $24,000 + $25,000 + $20,000 + $0) gives $207,080.72. The $64,248 Home Lumber deal (closed Jul 25, 2025) is counted in that account's card and its "~$90K" note, but excluded from every stated total — both stat cards and the manager takeaways. True recoverable ≈ $207.1K, not ≈$142.8K.

items.title: The ownership gap is already closed
items.body: Part 1 shows five accounts as — assign, unowned. As of today HubSpot has all seven owned: Pouyan Mirsaeidi (Home Lumber, Southern Tool, Randy's Hardware, Handy Ace Hardware) and Joshua Kolenda (Gold Beach Lumber, Family Hardware, KB Home Center). Assigned after the July 21, 2026 match date used in Part 1. "Close the ownership gap" is done — don't send Josh and Pouyan chasing a solved problem at the booth.

items.title: KB Home Center's Adyen blocker was already under internal review — status unconfirmed
items.body: Southern Tool Supply, Family Hardware, and KB Home Center all carry a rep-applied "Not in ICP" reason. KB Home Center's is explicit: "not in ICP - Adyen no[t] supported in Turks & Caicos" — a payments-rail limitation, not a sales objection. Gong calls add a material update: after the loss, Colton told the account he'd sent inquiries to Toolbx's own finance team about Adyen support and payment processing specifically for Turks & Caicos, and committed to share KB Home Center's account types and signatory needs with finance and product. That thread's outcome isn't in Gong — check with finance/product before the show whether Adyen coverage was actually extended. If yes, this account moves back up the priority order; if no, it's still a hard blocker and belongs in Skip alongside Mountain Mojo. Either way, this is a decision for the sales manager, not made here.

items.title: Southern Tool isn't as thin as Part 1 suggests
items.body: Part 1 flags Southern Tool Supply as "thin" with only 1 CRM contact. Gong calls surface at least one more named stakeholder — Brian Scott, actively exploring ERP alternatives to Epicor and familiar with Epicor's own Propello system — plus an unnamed AR/AP bookkeeping contact who confirmed interest in the payment portal, and an unspecified "powers that be" final-decision group. Add Brian Scott to CRM before the show; he's a warmer, more informed entry point than the single existing contact.

resolved.label: Both 2025 lost reasons
resolved.finding: $64,248 (Jul 25, 2025) — Lost communication / Unresponsive, rep note “unresponsive.” $26,388 (Oct 17, 2025) — Not Ready, rep note “not the right time.” Two different failure modes: the big one went dark, the small one was timing.

resolved.label: Whether the logged follow-up ever happened
resolved.finding: Partially confirmed via Gong: Jameson sent a meeting invite to Matt, and Matt confirmed receiving it. No subsequent call is on record, so whether the meeting itself actually took place is still unconfirmed — the follow-up action happened, the follow-up outcome didn't get captured.

resolved.label: Gong notes across the 6 contacts
resolved.finding: 5 calls found (Jan 2025–Jul 2026). Interest centered on the AR and payment portal, e-commerce, payment consolidation, increasing payment adoption, and reducing credit card fees. Objections raised: timing, needing to loop in the boss on pricing, risk of reintegration work if they switch ERPs, uncertainty about monthly cost increases after the initial term, inability to consolidate multiple customer accounts across stores, payment reconciliation friction, credit card fee cost, and customer adoption risk for new technology.

resolved.label: The May-2026 lost reason
resolved.finding: Not Ready; Other; Lack of prioritization. Scott's own note: “Pursuing other large IT projects and cannot put resources to this just now.”

resolved.label: What changed their mind
resolved.finding: Not pure capacity after all — Gong adds real texture (see 2c). Jason Fritz called the monthly fee "a little large," especially for the rental side, and Andrea Evans questioned ACH ROI given they don't have a collections problem. Both flagged "someone else to convince" internally, with a leadership presentation as a likely blocker. The lost-reason note's "pursuing other IT projects" was real, but a price/ROI question and an unresolved internal buy-in step were sitting underneath it — worth addressing both, not just timing, in the re-open.

resolved.label: Gong history with the 9 contacts
resolved.finding: 2 calls found. Jason Fritz and Andrea Evans were the primary voices. Objections: monthly fee felt large for the rental side; ACH ROI questioned without a collections problem to solve; internal permissions concerns; potential conflict between Toolbx and their existing "Do It Best" e-commerce site, specifically how special-order items not in Epicor would be handled; questions on integration time and pricing tiers across stores. Both contacts named a leadership presentation as the remaining internal hurdle.

resolved.label: The Oct-2025 lost reason
resolved.finding: Lost communication / Unresponsive; Lack of prioritization; Not in ICP. Colton's note: “went quiet.” Also carries a rep-applied “Not in ICP” flag — see correction C3.

resolved.label: The Jul-2 touch outcome
resolved.finding: Colton sent Brian Scott a link and login credentials to the customer-facing demo site for his team to explore, and the two planned to coordinate a follow-up meeting the following week. Positive, concrete next step — worth checking whether that follow-up meeting actually happened before the show.

resolved.label: Who else to add beyond the single contact
resolved.finding: Gong surfaces real names CRM doesn't have. Brian Scott is actively exploring ERP alternatives to Epicor. There's also an unnamed AR/AP bookkeeping contact who confirmed customer interest in a payment portal, and an unspecified "powers that be" group holding final say. See correction C4 and the CRM hygiene action to add Brian Scott.

resolved.label: Gong notes
resolved.finding: 1 call found. Colton walked through their current manual AR/collections process, then demoed the Toolbx customer portal (online payments, invoice visibility, order tracking) and the admin side (aged AR dashboard, automated payment requests). Brian Scott shared his experience with Epicor's Propello system and interest in alternatives.

resolved.label: The Oct-2025 lost reason
resolved.finding: Lack of prioritization; Lost communication / Unresponsive; Not in ICP. Colton's note: “went quiet (not good ICP).” Also carries a rep-applied “Not in ICP” flag — see correction C3.

resolved.label: Gong notes
resolved.finding: 1 call found. Jeremy Peterson (Owner) wants a B2B solution that lets customers view order history and easily repeat past orders. Colton noted Family Hardware currently runs on custom internal systems. No IHI interest surfaced — Jeremy asked about Toolbx's presence at a different show ("the best market"), which Colton confirmed Toolbx would attend.

That confirms she was the right contact at the time, not that she still is today — last recorded activity is Nov 3, 2025, so a quick freshness check before the show is still worth doing.

bullets: Deal and company data pulled live from HubSpot on July 28, 2026 (portal 49044619).
“Re-engage” is HubSpot custom lifecycle stage 1324949332 (Closed Lost – Re-engage), matching Part 1's usage.

Closed-lost reasons combine the `closed_lost_reasons` picklist and the `closed_lost_detail__c` free-text field — the latter is the rep's own words and is quoted verbatim, including one source typo (bracketed: “no[t]”).

Gong call data was pulled directly via the Gong MCP connector (ask_account, Jan 2025–Jul 28 2026) for all 7 accounts — 12 calls found in total. The Sales Hub connector's get_deal_gong_calls tool was tried first and returned 401 Unauthorized (interactive sign-in required, unavailable in this session) — the direct Gong connector was used instead and succeeded.

The two remaining open items (Family Hardware and KB Home Center attendance) were checked against the full Gong history and specifically against the Jun–Jul 2026 window — zero calls or emails mention IHI, NHPA, or trade-show attendance for either account. That absence is reported as a data point, not treated as confirmation of non-attendance; the pre-show campaign reply is still the real answer for both.

Corrections in this document were found by recomputing Part 1's own stated totals from its own per-account figures, by diffing Part 1's ownership/lifecycle claims against live HubSpot data, and by cross-checking Gong call content against both Part 1's and HubSpot's account framing.
Revenue / employee / branch figures from Part 1 were sourced from prior research and public sources there — treat as ±50%, unchanged from Part 1's own caveat.
